text: Group by collapses rows into one per group — sometimes you don't want that. Window functions.

Partition by plays the same role group by's columns did — it defines the groups. Order by decides the order within each one. Together they describe a neighborhood for every row, without actually collapsing anything yet.

Row number then numbers each row within its own partition, in the order specified — the highest fare per vendor gets rank one. Notice dot over — that's what tells Spark to apply the ranking per window instead of across the whole DataFrame.

And this properly solves Lesson 52's dropped-duplicates problem: rank the duplicates by whatever should decide the winner, then keep only the rows ranked number one — full control, instead of an arbitrary survivor.
Partition and order define the neighborhood, row number ranks within it, and every row survives. Next lesson: temporary views, for querying a DataFrame with real SQL.
